misclassified_entities.reason: Internal component - a smart contract calling the BLAKE2F precompile is executing within the EVM, part of the system under audit
Internal component - local configuration file read by the builder process, not an external entity sending data into the system
Internal component - protocol parameters are defined by the system specification, not external input
Environmental condition rather than an entity - network bandwidth is a physical constraint, not an actor sending data

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User or application submitting transactions. May submit malicious signatures with high s-values (blocked by EIP-2) or trigger request generation via contract execution. All signatures must be validated for low s-value. Transaction content must be validated against protocol rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Type-3 transactions with blob data from network mempool. Blobs are submitted by external users and must be validated for format, size, and KZG commitment. Blob data content cannot be trusted and may consume significant bandwidth during propagation.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Signature s-value must be validated to not exceed secp256k1n/2. All transaction fields must pass validation. High s-value signatures must be rejected to prevent transaction malleability.
Contract creation transactions require 53,000 gas minimum. Init code must be validated for length and gas consumption. Insufficient gas for code storage results in failure (not empty contract).
Transactions may trigger EL-to-CL request generation. Request data is committed via SHA256 hash. CL must validate requests independently; EL only provides integrity commitment.
Blob transactions in mempool must have valid KZG commitments. Builders must respect configured blob limits to ensure successful propagation. Excessive blobs can cause network propagation failures.
